name: Chris Campbell
bio: Chris Campbell of Bristol is an independent candidate for Tennessee's 1st Congressional District, listed on the Tennessee Secretary of State's 2026 candidate list. No campaign materials or prior public office were found.
notes: Searched news archives, statewide candidate guides and likely campaign domains; only his Bristol hometown was found (NewsChannel 5 guide). No website, social accounts or issue statements were found.

name: Adam Heimerman
bio: Adam Heimerman, 37, of Lenoir City is an independent candidate for Tennessee's 2nd Congressional District and has not held elected office. He is described in press coverage as a river guide and has been reported as a commercial photographer. In July 2026 he was arrested and charged with four felony vandalism counts over the shooting of license-plate reader cameras in Blount County; the case is pending.

platform.point: Pledges full federal funding for all national parks plus added money to protect and restore riparian zones.
Opposes selling public lands to private companies, saying taxpayers already paid for them.
Describes automated license-plate reader cameras as a sign the country is becoming a police state.

security.evidence: He told the Washington Post that license-plate reader cameras symbolize a slide toward a police state and that residents are frustrated with their continued use.

notes: Checked his YouTube channel (one campaign video, on national parks) and national coverage of his July 2026 arrest; no campaign website was found. Positions on the economy, immigration, abortion and most other topics remain unknown.

name: Dean Arnold
bio: Dean Arnold is an author, journalist and filmmaker from Chattanooga running as an independent in Tennessee's 3rd Congressional District. He moved to Chattanooga in 1982 to attend Covenant College, led the American Rights Coalition from 1988 to 1991, and published the weekly Chattanooga Fax from 1996 to 2004. He has said he was traditionally a Republican.

platform.point: Supports deporting people in the country illegally but says ICE agents who overstepped should be prosecuted.
Asked about the deficit, said he would have voted against the 2025 "Big Beautiful Bill."
Says Social Security was funded from workers' paychecks, is not an entitlement, and people deserve those benefits.
Argues the country needs a Christ-centered, biblical outlook to restore sanity to public life.
Says running as an independent frees him to criticize Israel, which he could not do as a Republican.
Said some close allies of President Trump, naming Pete Hegseth and Marco Rubio, should be prosecuted.

welfare.evidence: General statement: he said Social Security benefits were paid for out of paychecks and people deserve to receive them.

liberty.evidence: General: his campaign biography lists pro-life activism (abortion) among his past work; no statements on drugs, LGBTQ rights, guns or speech were found.

immigration.evidence: He told a Chattanooga civic club he favors deporting people here illegally, while calling immigration a case-by-case matter and saying ICE agents who overstepped should be prosecuted.

faith.evidence: He told the Chattanooga Civitans that sanity requires Jesus Christ at the center of what the country does and that a biblical view of the future is needed.

notes: Reviewed his campaign pages (which list no issues), personal sites, YouTube channel and a March 2026 Chattanoogan.com report of a Civitan Club talk, where he said he had no platform yet. Positions on the economy, energy, technology, security and education remain unknown.

name: Jean Howard-Hill
bio: Jean Howard-Hill is an independent candidate for Tennessee's 3rd Congressional District from Chattanooga. She is a retired college professor and business consultant with a degree from Wheaton College, and a Republican activist who has run for this seat several times, including in 2004, 2008, 2010 and 2024.

platform.point: Pledges nonpartisan cooperation and an open-door office for all residents of the district.

notes: Very little current issue information was found; the one platform item comes from Vote Smart and may date from an earlier campaign. A new search of news archives, statewide candidate guides and likely campaign domains found no 2026 statements (the Facebook page requires a login).

name: Rodney King
current_role: Retired Navy officer and former teacher
bio: Rodney Joe King, born in Jefferson City in 1955, is an independent candidate for Tennessee's 3rd Congressional District from Powell. He is a retired U.S. Navy officer who served as a submarine and nuclear weapons officer, then taught science for 20 years, mostly in Oak Ridge public schools, where he coached a robotics team.

platform.point: Supports universal health care, citing insurer profits and administrative costs, and calls ACA subsidies a poor deal.
Wants Social Security fully funded, with the wealthiest who received tax breaks helping pay for it.
Calls for lower taxes on working Americans and criticizes the 2025 tax law's permanent cuts for billionaires.
States that he believes in the "Right to Life" and supports the Second Amendment.
Says no war should begin without approval from Congress.
Backs the strongest possible ban on stock trading by members of Congress and pledges not to trade.
Wants the federal government out of student lending, saying degrees should be financed by the students.
Calls himself an environmentalist and stresses protecting clean air, water and land.

economy.evidence: His campaign site calls for the wealthiest to pay more toward Social Security, criticizes permanent tax cuts for billionaires, and backs lower taxes on working Americans.

welfare.evidence: His campaign site supports universal health care and full funding of Social Security.

liberty.evidence: His site says he believes in the "Right to Life" (abortion, toward community norms) and supports the Second Amendment (guns, toward individual choice).

foreign.evidence: General statement: his site says no war should start without congressional approval, stressing caution before sending troops into harm's way.

energy.evidence: General statement: he calls himself an unapologetic environmentalist committed to clean air, water and land, without naming energy policies.

notes: Found and read his campaign website (a single platform page; the About and Contact pages hold only template text). No positions were found on immigration, security, technology, K-12 education or faith in public life.

name: Donnie Ownby
bio: Donnie Lynn Ownby is an independent candidate for Tennessee's 3rd Congressional District, listed by the state as living in Philadelphia, Tennessee. He is described as a businessman and U.S. Army veteran.
notes: A new search of news archives, statewide candidate guides and likely campaign domains found no website, social accounts or issue statements. The businessman and Army veteran description comes from the first research round.
